manchete.titulo: MoMA to Host First US Ana Mendieta Retrospective in Over 20 Years
manchete.resumo: The indelible impact of late Cuban-American artist Ana Mendieta 's practice will be celebrated in a forthcoming retrospective in New York next year. Scheduled to open at the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) in Manhattan in…
manchete.trecho: The indelible impact of late Cuban-American artist Ana Mendieta 's practice will be celebrated in a forthcoming retrospective in New York next year. Scheduled to open at the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) in Manhattan in December 2027, Ana Mendieta: A Retrospective marks the first presentation of Mendieta's overarching career in the United States in over 20 years. MoMA's announcement comes just two months before Tate Modern's ongoing Mendieta retrospective closes in London. Comprising around 200 works, including rarely seen formative drawings and newly remastered films, the MoMA exhibition will present Mendieta's artistic process, signature developments, and career milestones in a chronological fashion. Starting with early figurative works completed during her undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Iowa, the exhibition will follow the artist's subsequent expansion in…

noticias.titulo: 98 Years Ago, This 7 Min Cartoon Changed Hollywood Animation Forever
noticias.resumo: On November 18, 1928, audiences at New York City’s Colony Theater were the first to have their lives changed forever. They thought they were seated to see a war drama called Gang War. But before the main titles rolled…
noticias.trecho: On November 18, 1928, audiences at New York City’s Colony Theater were the first to have their lives changed forever. They thought they were seated to see a war drama called Gang War. But before the main titles rolled, they were treated to a surprise cartoon. Many of them probably wondered what the hell a cartoon is, but that's beside the point. The point is that suddenly the lights went down, then music rolled, and a talkie animated short played about a mouse on a steamboat that was written, directed, and animated by a guy named Walt Disney . He was a once-in-a-generation genius who was about to embark on one of the most storied film careers of all time. Now, ninety-eight years later, Steamboat Willie is remembered as the landmark moment animation found its voice and its fiercest advocate, along with its most famous character. noticias.trecho: a new timber district takes shape in Thun   Bjarke Ingels Group / BIG unveils plans for four timber buildings in Thun, Switzerland , where the architecture firm will help shape the entrance to the city’s emerging Siegenthalergut district. The 13,000-square-meter development brings together two hotels and residential buildings, with stacked wooden volumes that project outward above the street. Set against the Bernese Alps, the architecture is defined by deep window grids and large terraces carved into the buildings’ stepped facades.   The proposal, developed with landscape architects August + Margrith Künzel, was selected through a competition organized by Frutiger AG and the city of Thun. Titled Nachwachsende Stadt, or Growing City, the scheme occupies one of the first two plots planned for the new neighborhood. The small building stands on a one-acre site in Wilson, Wyoming, located just beyond the popular ski town of Jackson . The site is dotted with mature trees and sits along the west bank of the Snake River. Before the project's inception, the clients had lived on the property for 25 years – in a modest, 1960s house they had renovated – and had raised their son there. As their son neared graduation from high school, the couple decided to build an ADU on the property and make it their full-time residence, while renting out the main residence. referencias.titulo: Hand-Marbled Papers Ground Sylvain Lefebvre’s Surreal Landscapes
referencias.resumo: Enormous trees dominate dreamlike wooded landscapes in the mixed-media paintings of Sylvain Lefebvre . A spectral form with dense, gnarly branches shelters a lounging woman in “The Quercus Corallium,” and a table alive…
referencias.trecho: Enormous trees dominate dreamlike wooded landscapes in the mixed-media paintings of Sylvain Lefebvre . A spectral form with dense, gnarly branches shelters a lounging woman in “The Quercus Corallium,” and a table alive with conversation nests beneath the canopy in “A Debat at Tea Time.” The French artist’s Journeys Into the Unseen Forest at Rebecca Hossack Art Gallery comprises a series of almost fairytale-like tableaux. Collaged, hand-marbled papers beneath the delicate layers of oil paint represent the barely visible or unknown. And trees group closely in the background darken in the distance, while diminutive figures climb around and relax at the base of monumental trunks. “The Polyphane Pachidermus” (2026), oil, acrylic, and ink on hand-painted marbled paper, on canvas, 120 x 160 centimeters Summer 2026 marked France’s hottest ever documented since records began, during which…

referencias.titulo: The Cutest Dancing Smart Speaker That Never Was
referencias.resumo: In 2018, AI/smart hardware startup Raven Tech collaborated with Teenage Engineering on the prototype for Raven R, a dancing smart speaker. Now, thanks to 3D motion designer Peter Pongó, we get a glimpse at its secret…
referencias.trecho: In 2018, AI/smart hardware startup Raven Tech collaborated with Teenage Engineering on the prototype for Raven R, a dancing smart speaker. Now, thanks to 3D motion designer Peter Pongó, we get a glimpse at its secret inner life. Peter Pongó: The Raven R was never commercially released so I brought it back from the grave as a dancing robot motion piece. I’ve always felt it deserved better than a shelf in the archive. I wanted to show how the Raven R can play on people’s feelings: how movement, rhythm, and sound can make a audience care about something that is, on paper, just a machine. This is the perfect subject because it doesn’t just play music, it is supposed to perform it.         Director/animator: Peter Pongó Background art: Jerry-Lee Bosmans The post The Cutest Dancing Smart Speaker That Never Was appeared first on Motion design - STASH .

biblioteca.titulo: Por meio de modos e espaços: dos movimentos migratórios da comunicação
biblioteca.resumo: Os Espaços da Comunicação , de Roger Odin, exercita um método minucioso de análise dos mais variados fenômenos da comunicação humana, com ênfase no cinema expandido e no audiovisual. Nesse sentido, o trabalho de Odin…
biblioteca.trecho: Os Espaços da Comunicação , de Roger Odin, exercita um método minucioso de análise dos mais variados fenômenos da comunicação humana, com ênfase no cinema expandido e no audiovisual. Nesse sentido, o trabalho de Odin remete a obras como Fundamentos da Teoria dos Signos , publicado em 1976, de Charles W. Morris, originalmente publicado em 1938. Nesse trabalho, Morris se aprofunda na dimensão pragmática da linguagem e da comunicação. De certa maneira, Odin atualiza o interesse pela dimensão pragmática com sua semiopragmática, recombinando instrumentos de análise dos processos comunicacionais. Com rigor e desprendimento, Odin oferece um modelo teórico atento às particularidades da Comunicação de seu tempo.

bolhas.titulo: Artist Notes: “The Kitchen Table” by Sin Wai Kin
bolhas.resumo: Dinner is ready. I come downstairs, wipe the table, and set it with napkins and chopsticks. Dishes arrive in the middle. A steamed red snapper, braised bak choy and shiitake mushrooms, a white cut chicken with ginger…
bolhas.trecho: Dinner is ready. I come downstairs, wipe the table, and set it with napkins and chopsticks. Dishes arrive in the middle. A steamed red snapper, braised bak choy and shiitake mushrooms, a white cut chicken with ginger scallion sauce. Three bowls of rice. My mother and father sit across from each other at the table. I sit between them, across from the north-facing window which the table sits against.  Outside the window there is only a white void.  The kitchen table is also white, the walls are also white, the chairs we sit on are also white. All these objects form our context, the support for the food, our bodies, our shelter, our lives that facilitate this family meal. The whiteness fades into the background but it is the reality that we eat in. I am so used to it that I don’t see it, even as it contrasts with the cobalt blue ornamenting the dish that the steamed fish lies in. My mother…
